topics.headline: Oil surge and energy pass-through favor both CPI and HICP rising
topics.summary: Brent's climb toward $89 amid Iran/Houthi supply threats, plus economist previews (PNC, Barclays) arguing gasoline declines won't repeat, point to a likely rebound in both July US CPI and Eurozone HICP after June's dip; ECB's own projections and Lagarde's second-round-effects warning reinforce the case, though low-liquidity prediction markets (48.5% YES) show real uncertainty remains.

topics.headline: HY OAS tight at 2.77%, but private credit stress signals brewing
topics.summary: Headline high-yield spreads remain historically tight and stable even as rate volatility and Middle East tensions push Treasury yields higher, but mounting private credit/BDC distress (redemption caps, NAV cuts, rising defaults) mirrors the early-2026 pattern that preceded a 50bp HY spread widening—suggesting risk of contagion into public HY OAS over the next 30 days even though no acute break has occurred yet.

topics.headline: BTC ETF inflow streak breaks as FOMC decision looms
topics.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs snapped a seven-day inflow run with $225-240M in outflows on July 24, and with BTC hovering near $64K in "fear" territory heading into the July 28-29 FOMC decision (rates expected to hold), the next 7 days hinge on whether that outflow was a one-off geopolitical blip or the start of a renewed downtrend.

topics.headline: VIX term structure and catalysts point to higher volatility ahead
topics.summary: VIX sits at 18.58 but futures in contango (VIX3M 20.51) signal markets expect it to rise, backed by a semiconductor selloff, escalating US-Iran conflict, and fresh Trump tariffs on Canada/China; with hawkish Fed signals adding fuel, odds favor VIX finishing above its 3-month average in 30 days.

topics.headline: Deal pace stays torrid despite NY moratorium and grid pushback
topics.summary: Chevron-Microsoft's 20-year Pecos power deal, Digital Realty's Kansas City agreement, and GE Vernova's surging turbine backlog show hyperscaler power deals are still landing at a rapid clip, even as New York's data-center moratorium and Texas' new ERCOT load-review process signal rising regulatory friction.
